entities.name: Nizam al-Din al-Nisaburi
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Nizam al-Din Hasan al-Nisaburi, a towering polymath of the early 14th century Ilkhanate, epitomized the intellectual vigor of Persian Islamic scholarship, synthesizing rational and transmitted sciences. Flourishing until his death in 1328, al-Nisaburi excelled across an astonishing array of disciplines including mathematics, astronomy, jurisprudence, Qur'anic exegesis, and poetry. His profound contributions helped sustain and advance the rigorous intellectual traditions established during the Islamic Golden Age, even as the Mongol-era political landscape transformed the Near East, making him a critical figure in the transmission of knowledge.

Al-Nisaburi's magnum opus, "Ghara'ib al-Qur'an wa Ragha'ib al-Furqan" (Wonders of the Qur'an and Desires of the Criterion), stands as one of the most comprehensive and widely studied Qur'an commentaries, integrating linguistic, theological, legal, and even scientific insights. In astronomy, he produced "Sharh al-Tajrid," a commentary on Nasir al-Din al-Tusi's "Tajrid al-Kalam," and made significant advancements in the field of spherical trigonometry. His mathematical prowess was further demonstrated through commentaries on Euclid's "Elements," solidifying his reputation as a master of both theoretical and applied sciences, often working from intellectual centers like Nishapur and Tabriz during the Mongol peace.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Nizam al-Din al-Nisaburi's comprehensive Qur'an commentary and advanced scientific treatises ensured the transmission and development of critical Islamic scholarship for centuries, profoundly influencing intellectual traditions from the Ilkhanate to the Ottoman Empire.
